When it feels smooth or starts to tear. For players on court every week that is usually every few weeks.

description: Racket bags, backpacks and holdalls with room for the whole kit.

metafields.seo_text:

title: Padel balls
description: Tubes and boxes from the brands used at clubs and tournaments.

metafields.seo_text:
Padel balls look like tennis balls but run at a lower pressure, so they bounce less and suit the enclosed court.
Balls lose pressure once the tube is opened. Most players change them every few sessions.
faq: Can I use tennis balls?
They will work, but they bounce too high. Padel balls are made at a lower pressure for the court.
How long do padel balls last?
Usually a few sessions once opened. You will notice them bouncing lower and feeling heavy.

title: Padel rackets
description: Find the right racket for your game.

metafields.seo_heading: Choosing a racket for your level
metafields.seo_text:
Every padel racket we sell is chosen from the brands players trust most, from Bullpadel and Nox in Spain to Head, Babolat and Adidas. Each one is tagged with a level, a shape and a weight so you can compare like for like.
If you are new to the game, start with a round racket and a soft core. Regular players looking for more power should look at teardrop and hybrid shapes, while competitive players tend to choose diamond shapes with firmer cores and carbon faces.
Not sure where you fit? Our racket guide explains shape, balance, core and face materials in plain English.
faq: Which padel racket should I buy as a beginner?
Start with a round racket with a soft core. It has the biggest sweet spot and is the easiest to control while you learn.
What is the difference between round, teardrop and diamond?
Round shapes keep the weight low for control. Diamond shapes put the weight in the head for power. Teardrop sits in between.
How heavy should my racket be?
Most players use a racket between 355 and 375g. Lighter rackets are easier to swing and kinder on the arm.

title: Padel shoes
description: Grip, support and comfort for every court surface.

metafields.seo_text:
Padel shoes are built for quick lateral movement. Most courts in the UK are artificial grass with sand, which suits a herringbone or omni sole. Clay soles suit very sandy courts.
Look for a firm heel, good support at the side of the foot and a sole that grips without sticking.
faq: Can I play padel in running shoes?
It is not a good idea. Running shoes are built to move forwards, not side to side, and the sole will not grip a sandy court.
Which sole should I choose?
Herringbone and omni soles suit most UK courts. Choose clay if your club's courts are very sandy.
